content:
Request Refinery — Field Journal (notes for engineering/product handoff)

Document purpose:
- Quickly capture customer examples and pragmatic remediation ideas from Nov 2–9 field engagements.
- Produce a compact handoff to serving-runtime and product with concrete patches we can prototype in a sprint.

Topline themes observed (frequency-wins):
1) Unexpected latency spikes for small interactive calls
   - Trigger: customers using short prompt completions (few tokens) seeing 200–800ms variance when backend batches with larger sequences.
   - Quote: "Our live chat is jittery — sometimes answers come instantly, sometimes they lag a second or two, which is noticeable to end-users." — Acme Health engineer
2) Confusion over billing for mixed workloads
   - Trigger: teams sending embedding + generation within same session see combined token charges and are unsure about unit mapping.
   - Quote: "Why did a 12-token call to vectorize cost the same as a short generation? We need clearer charge breakdowns." — BlueCart product manager
3) Edge routing surprises at peak
   - Trigger: smart routing fallback moves to a quantized model variant that introduces higher hallucination risk for certain prompt families.
   - Quote: "Fallback is keeping us online but the answers are worse; can we control which variants are acceptable?" — Codex Labs ML lead
4) Preference for per-route quick toggles and playable fallbacks in Console
   - Teams want buttons: enable/disable caching, force low-latency route, set failover to read-only model, etc.

Raw customer vignettes (short):
- Acme Health: Short triage flows (3–8 tokens) used across telehealth triage. They want 90th percentile p95 < 250ms. They are willing to accept a minor quality drop for deterministic latency.
- BlueCart: Mixed pipeline (embedding + chat) where billing clarity = procurement blocker. Wants an exportable per-request cost line-item.
- Codex Labs: Uses code-completion model variants. When routing falls back to smaller quantized model, they see broken code formatting. They asked for a whitelist of acceptable fallback variants per route.
- Neptune Retail: Observed KV-cache cold-starts when traffic shifts between routes; want pre-warming heuristics or explicit cache pinning for high-value routes.

Proposed microfixes (low-effort, quick ROI):
A) Quick small-batch bypass mode (hosted): route requests < N tokens to dedicated low-latency worker that disables cross-request batching for those callers.
   - Rationale: restores consistent latency at the cost of throughput; acceptable for interactive products.
   - Estimated effort: 1.5–2 weeks (routing + config flag + metrics).
   - Risks: increased cost for small calls; must surface in Console and billing dashboard.
B) Per-request cost breakdown header in API response (beta)
   - Rationale: immediate visibility for customers doing mixed embeddings/generation.
   - Estimated effort: 3–5 days (API change + Console display).
   - Risks: minor churn for SDKs; ensure forward/backwards compat.
C) Fallback whitelist per route (Console + policy)
   - Rationale: give customers control over which model variants are allowed as fallbacks to avoid quality regressions.
   - Estimated effort: 2–3 weeks (policy surface + enforcement).

Prioritization note: quick small-batch bypass (A) and per-request cost header (B) appear to unblock multiple customers immediately and reduce support load. Fallback whitelist (C) is higher engineering cost but reduces churn for heavy product customers.

Engineering hooks & metrics to track during spike experiments:
- End-to-end latency p50/p90/p95 for short (<10 token) calls
- Rate of fallback events by route & model variant
- Regression checks on hallucination / perplexity for fallbacks (sampled evaluation sets)
- Billing mismatch reports (number of queries flagged for ambiguous charge split)

Open questions (need discipline before spike):
- What should N be for small-batch bypass? Suggest starting at 12 tokens and tuning from live traffic.
- How do we surface the cost delta for users who default to bypass mode? (soft warning in Console, API header, and billing export)
- Are there existing quotas or tenant isolation constraints that block a dedicated low-latency worker per-tenant?

Next steps & owners (recommended):
- Product: Priya Patel — own requirements doc & acceptance criteria for per-request cost header (1 week).
- Serving Runtime: Diego Morales — spike small-batch bypass routing (2 weeks) and produce perf numbers.
- Console: Liam O'Rourke — mockups for fallback whitelist UI and cost visibility screens (5 days).
- CS: Maya Chen — coordinate pilot with Acme Health and BlueCart, collect p95 telemetry and user sentiment.

Pilot plan (2-week pilot):
Week 1: deploy per-request cost header to beta tenants + small-batch bypass behind feature flag; collect perf and billing telemetry.
Week 2: enable fallback whitelist for pilot tenants, run manual evals on sample prompt sets, gather customer sign-off.

Checklist before pilot:
- [ ] API header schema finalized and SDK chips noted
- [ ] Flag gating for low-latency worker created and documented
- [ ] Deployment plan with rollback points and canary percentages
- [ ] Eval harness defined for fallback regressions (reference prompt set)

Appendix: Suggested sample JIRA tickets to create
- CS-2034: Implement small-batch bypass routing for short calls (owner: Diego)
- CS-2140: Add per-request cost breakdown header + Console view (owner: Priya)
- CS-2185: Fallback whitelist policy and Console control (owner: Liam)

Notes to self:
- Keep this document iterative — will update after pilot.
- Push clear telemetry exports to S3 for CS consumption (daily rolling windows).

End of journal entry.
